sentences.text: By way of the present application under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, the applicant-accused has prayed for enlarging him on Anticipatory Bail in connection with the FIR being C.R. No. 11191048230463 of 2023 registered wit h Sarkhej Police Station, Ahmedabad City for the offences punishable under Sections 406, 420, 465, 467, 468, 471, 120B of the Indian Penal Code.

2. Heard learned advocate Mr.A.S.Timbalia appearing for the applicant and learned APP Mr.T.C.Kathiriya for the respondent State.
3.
Learned advocate for the applicant submitted that the incident alleged in the FIR had occurred during the period between 27.5.2022 to 2.6.2023, for which the FIR came to be lodged on 2.6.2023.

Thus, the FIR came to be lodged by NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/23238/2023 ORDER DATED:
12/06/2024 undefined the first informant after delay of considerable period.

sentences.text: 4. As per the case of prosecution, the present applicant along with the other co-accused got executed two Power of Attorneys in favour of the wife of the first informant.
The signature of the first informant on the said Power of Attorneys was allegedly forged.

On the basis of the said Power of Attorneys, which were executed in favour of the wife of the first informant, she had executed two different agreements to sale, qua two parcels of land belonging to the first informant in favour of the co-accused and for the said agreements to sale, the amount of consideration has also been received by the wife of the first informant.
However, interestingly, in the present offence, the wife of the first informant has not been arraigned as an accused for the reasons best known to the first informant.
The present applicant is a lady, who has not received any financial gain out of the transactions in question.
The FIR in question has been lodged by the first informant with some ulterior motive after a delay of almost four years from the date of alleged incident.
He, therefore, submitted to allow the present application and enlarge the present applicant on bail subject to suitable conditions.
5. The application is opposed by learned APP Mr.Trupesh C. Kathiriya inter alia
contending

that the present applicant has not made herself available for the purpose of investigation and therefore, a warrant under Section 70 of the Cr.P.C. had been NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/23238/2023 ORDER DATED: 12/06/2024 undefined issued against her.

The applicant has been getting herself away from the process of investigation and therefore, as per the settled legal position, the discretionary relief of Anticipatory Bail should not be granted to the present applicant.
5.1
Learned APP seeks to rely upon the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Prem Shankar Prasad Vs. State of Bihar [(2022) 14 SCC 516].

sentences.text: He therefore, submitted that the present applicant has played an active role in connivance with the other co-accused in the present offence.
He therefore submitted to dismiss the present application.

6. Learned advocate Mr.Dipen Desai appearing for the original complainant has also opposed the present application contending that the present applicant has another antecedent for commission of similar nature of offence and in the said offence also, FIR came to be lodged by the present first informant.

In the said offence, the applicant was ordered to be enlarged on regular bail, however,
since, after being enlarged on regular bail, the applicant did not remain present before the concerned trial court and therefore, a non-bailable warrant came to be issued upon her.
In the present offence also warrant under Section 70 of the Cr.P.C.
has been issued against the applicant.
Therefore, the discretion should not be exercised in favour of the present applicant.

He submitted that the present applicant along with the other co-accused had taken advantage of the ailment of the wife of the first informant and had got executed two Power of Attorneys with a forged signature of the first informant in favour of his ailing wife.

The wife, in turn, had executed two different agreements to sale qua different parcels of NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/23238/2023 ORDER DATED: 12/06/2024 undefined land belonging to the first informant in favour of the other co-accused.
The present applicant has received monetary gain out of the entire transaction.

He submitted that the application filed by the other co-accused for Anticipatory Bail has been dismissed by the Co-ordinate Bench of this court and therefore, the present application should also be dismissed.

sentences.text: Heard learned Advocates for the parties and perused the record.
At the outset, the conduct of the present applicant is required to be taken note of.
The present FIR has been registered on 2.6.2023.
After the registration of the offence, the investigating agency has made several attempts to secure the presence of the present applicant.
Even notices under Section 41A of the Cr.P.C. have also been issued asking her to appear before the investigating agency.

However, the present applicant has defied all such notices and summons issued by the investigating agency and therefore, as a last resort, a warrant under Section 70 of the Cr.P.C. came to be issued against her.
This indicates that the present applicant is evading the process of law.

7.1 The Hon'ble Apex Court in its judgment in the case of Prem Shankar Prasad (supra) has held that when the accused is absconding and declared as a proclaimed offender, the Anticipatory Bail cannot be granted.
Not only this, in another offence wherein, FIR has been lodged by the present first informant, the applicant had been arraigned as an accused and was arrested during the course of investigation.
In the said offence, which is of NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/23238/2023 ORDER DATED: 12/06/2024 undefined similar nature, the applicant was ordered to be enlarged on regular bail.
However, after being enlarged on bail, the applicant did not remain present before the trial court and therefore, a non-bailable warrant came to be issued against her.
This shows the tendency on part of the applicant of evading the process of law.
8. So far as the merits of the matter is concerned, the wife of the first informant was suffering from physical and mental ailment.
The applicant along with the other co- accused had taken advantage of this situation and had got executed two Power of Attorneys in favour of the ailing wife of the first informant.
The signatures of the first informant on both the Power of Attorneys were forged, as per the report of the hand-writing expert collected during the course of investigation.

The present applicant along with the other co-accused, made the ailing wife of the first informant execute two different agreements to sale in favour of the co-accused on the basis of aforesaid two forged Power of Attorneys.
8.1 The record further indicates that the present applicant got open a separate bank account of the wife of the first informant.
The mobile number belonging to the present applicant had been attached to the said account.

The other co-accused, after the agreements to sale were executed, had deposited the amount of consideration in the said bank account, which was withdrawn by the applicant thereafter and was returned to the said co-accused.

Thus, the applicant appears to have played an active role in NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/23238/2023 ORDER DATED: 12/06/2024 undefined commission of the offence in question.
9.

The fact that the first informant in the present case has also lodged another FIR against the present applicant, wherein she was arrested, indicates that the applicant had a criminal track record for commission of similar nature of offence.
10. Considering all these aspects, no case is made out to exercise discretion in favour of the applicant.
Accordingly, the present Application is dismissed.
